title: Enable screen help on Linux
goal: The GUI helper runs in your desktop session and reports ready

steps.title: What screen help means
steps.text: With your approval per task I can take screenshots and use mouse and keyboard in the apps you name. An overlay shows while I am in control, and a stop hotkey ends it at once.

steps.title: X11 has no permission prompt
steps.text: On X11 any program can see the screen and send input, so the hub's grant is the only gate. A Wayland session asks you through the desktop first.

steps.title: Start the GUI helper in your session
steps.text: Run this in a terminal inside your desktop session. To start it at login, add --autostart (writes an XDG autostart entry).
steps.check: The machine page shows GUI permission states

steps.title: Approve the desktop's screen sharing dialog (Wayland)
steps.text: On Wayland your desktop asks to share the screen and allow remote input. Approve it; the helper keeps a single-use restore token (0600) so you are not asked every time.

steps.title: Ready
steps.text: Screen help is ready. Each task still needs a gui-assist access card. On wlroots desktops input is reported unsupported and only capture works.
